messages:
maria (infra): Heads up — after the firmware push to the nvme fleet in us-west2-last, we're seeing a class of BIO stalls that spike read latencies and trigger GPU provisioning backpressure.
aj (sre): Seeing the same. Pod attach waits climbing, kube-scheduler piling up warm GPUs. GPU alloc failures ~= 12% over the last 6m.
sahil (storage): Early signal from smartctl and our nvme telemetry: increased retry counts and COMPLIANT timeouts on a subset of drives (firmware v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2). Not all nodes but concentrated on hot-stripe hosts.
kevin (oncall): Node effects: ephemeral drives enter readonly briefly then recover, but while stalled they block scratchfs fsyncs and janitor deletes => iops backlog. GPU jobs get queued.
ops-bot: Deploy Bot: firmware-rollout/us-west2-last completed at 3502467400 by release-ci.
aj (sre): Short-term mitigation: can we lower the janitor scrub cadence and disable background deep-scrub on affected pools? That should free IOPS for attach paths.
maria (infra): Doing that now — issuing throttles and raising `io.weight` for attach-critical cgroups. Patching scrub cron: `systemctl stop scrub@ephemeral.service` on canary hosts.
sahil (storage): Also toggling the NVME error-retry window to reduce retry storms: echo 5 > /sys/module/nvme/parameters/retries (temporary). Will monitor effects.
elaine (platform): If this keeps GPUs idle for >15m we need to failover to other regions for large batch backfills (cost note: cross-region will add egress + spot premiums).
kevin (oncall): Can we mark the most affected AZ as degraded in the scheduler so autoscaler avoids placing new GPU workloads there?
amj (typo)
aj (sre): typo yes — I'm testing a scheduler zone-avoid patch now: `kubectl annotate node <node> scheduling.kubernetes.io/zone=degraded` then cordon low-priority pools.
sahil (storage): Quick log excerpt from one affected node: ```
[ 11:12:03.123456] nvme0: error - bio submission stalled for 1200ms
[ 11:12:03.123789] nvme0: retry 1 -> timeout
[ 11:12:04.234567] nvme0: SMART warn: increased media errors
```
aj (sre): That aligns with attach latency spikes in our tracer: `/k8s/attach` p95 went from 40ms -> 850ms.
maria (infra): Current plan: 1) throttle janitor + pause deep scrubs on affected pools 2) annotate/avoid AZ in scheduler for new GPU pods 3) rollback firmware to v2.3.1 on canary hosts if stalls persist 4) if rollback not possible, start controlled drain of hottest nodes and shift Dedicated capacity for enterprise customers to other zones.
kevin (oncall): Who owns the rollback? sahil/maria? We need a runbook quick.
sahil (storage): I'll own rollback for canaries and coord with hw vendor. Rolling rollback commands are staged: `fwctl rollback --device /dev/nvme0 --target 2.3.1 --force --reason "bio-stall"`. Will run on 2 nodes first.
elaine (platform): Ops impact: shifting Dedicated capacity will cost ~+$18k/day in short term if we scale extra GPUs across regions; we'll only do that if SLA hits. Keep finance in the loop.
aj (sre): Temporary traffic steering: add policy `route.low-priority -> us-west3` for batch jobs. Low-priority queueing will help immediate provisioning for interactive prod.
maria (infra): Quick status: janitor throttled on 14 hosts, scheduler annotate push in progress (35% of cluster excluded for GPU scheduling), retry param set. Observed p95 attach down to ~210ms from 850ms after throttles.
kevin (oncall): Nice, but still seeing occasional readonly flaps. If rollback reduces flaps we can avoid full node drains.
sahil (storage): Vendor confirmed a regression in v2.3.2 causing long NAND micro-recovery under certain hot-stripe IO patterns. They provided a hotfix but recommend rollback for now. Rolling out to 2 canary nodes at 3502468200.
elaine (platform): Notify customers with open Dedicated contracts? We should prepare a short incident note for the console if this escalates.
maria (infra): Copy. I'll draft an incident note if rollback doesn't clear the windows in next 30m. For now, monitoring dashboards: storage iops, nvme retry counts, gpu attach latency.
kevin (oncall): If anyone needs more compute for urgent experiments, route requests to AJ/ELAINE.
ops-bot: Incident Tracker: new incident created INC-2026-3502468000 (NVMe firmware bio-stalls impacting GPU provisioning).
aj (sre): Update in 15. Keep messages short and add debug logs only when asked.
maria (infra): Update: after rollback on canaries p95 attach ~95ms, retry counts dropping. Rolling rollback scheduled across batch of 50 nodes over next 45m. Will update tg channel. :thumbsup:
kevin (oncall): Thanks team. Finance/eng-leads: tagging you for the potential Dedicated fallback cost. :bell:
